title: Advanced 4 · Ring modulation
text:
A ring modulator multiplies two signals. Multiplying two tones doesn't give you either of them: it gives their sum and their difference. A 200 Hz and a 300 Hz make 500 Hz and 100 Hz. Those are rarely in tune with the note you play, which is why ring mod sounds like bells, metal and robots. Here the second oscillator is tuned 7 semitones (a fifth) above the first.

Try: its TUNE at 12 (an octave: the result is in tune, hollow); at 0 (the same note: an octave up, the difference is silence); at 6.3 or 3.3 (out of tune: clangs); unplug MIDI In's PITCH from the second oscillator so it stays on one note while the first follows your keys: every key now has a different, unrelated tone (the classic robot voice); plug an LFO into B instead of the oscillator (slow: tremolo; fast: growl); the ring mod's MIX to blend the plain tone back in.
